- A **red dot** (🔴) app"},{"id":"p14s2","text":"ears next to "DSH Update" in the Settings sidebar when a new version exists.
- "Update via npm" runs"},{"id":"p14s3","text":" `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@latest` with live progress (bar + the last
few lines of npm output"},{"id":"p14s4","text":"). There is deliberately **no scrolling log panel** — the full npm output
is written to `$DSH_HOME/p"},{"id":"p14s5","text":"lugin-data/dsh-updater-npm/last-run.log` when the operation ends, so
the card stays quiet and the lo"},{"id":"p14s6","text":"g is still there when you need it.
- When the update finishes, a **"Restart DSH"** button appears: i"},{"id":"p14s7","text":"t exits the current process with
the original command line and relaunches it (PowerShell on Windows,"},{"id":"p14s8","text":" `/bin/sh` on macOS/Linux).
The same button appears after source-tree updates and deployment repairs"},{"id":"p14s9","text":".
**No new activation URL is needed** — the browser re-authenticates by itself and no new window pop"},{"id":"p14s10","text":"s up.
- Once a swap succeeded (i.e. the new version is actually running) the card shows the **rollba"},{"id":"p14s11","text":"ck
point's disk usage** and a **"Remove rollback point"** button. The previous deployment is kept as"},{"id":"p14s12","text":"
`<sibling of install dir>/dsh.old-<timestamp>` (222 MB in a real case). Safety rule, enforced on
th"},{"id":"p14s13","text":"e host: only rollback points whose **version differs from the running version** are listed and
delet"},{"id":"p14s14","text":"ed — the live deployment is never touched.
- Version comparison is semver-style: a local version new"},{"id":"p14s15","text":"er than the remote one (e.g. rc.7 vs rc.6)
is not reported as an update."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"### Timeout policy and run log (since v1.12)"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"Older versions used a blunt 10-minute hard timeout for npm installs. On a slow link a staged install"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"
was measured downloading 247 tarballs (231 of the 239 `@deepseek-ai` sub-packages of a 222 MB tree)"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"
in 9 min 25 s and was then killed, reporting just `staging install failed: npm` — **not a hang, not"},{"id":"p16s4","text":" a
broken network, simply a hard timeout**."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"The watchdog is now two-threshold, and configurable through
`$DSH_HOME/plugin-data/dsh-updater-npm/c"},{"id":"p17s2","text":" is now two-threshold, and configurable through
`$DSH_HOME/plugin-data/dsh-updater-npm/config.json`:"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"| Key | Default | Meaning |"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"| `npmIdleMinutes` | `10` | minutes of **zero activity** before it is declared stuck and terminated "},{"id":"p20s2","text":"(slow but moving ⇒ never killed) |
| `npmTimeoutMinutes` | `60` | absolute wall-clock ceiling, to st"},{"id":"p20s3","text":"op a truly unbounded hang |"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"**What counts as activity (corrected in v1.12.1):** watching the child's stdout alone is not enough "},{"id":"p21s2","text":"—
npm prints almost nothing when it is not attached to a TTY (one measured 5-minute install produced"},{"id":"p21s3","text":"
**not a single stdout line** while npm's own debug log recorded 525 requests, and the watchdog kill"},{"id":"p21s4","text":"ed
it). Three signals are now combined, and the maximum wins:"},{"id":"p22s1","text":"1. `--loglevel=http` — npm logs every request/stage to stdout (measured: 1111 lines instead of 0);
2"},{"id":"p22s2","text":". `--logs-dir` — npm's full debug log is written to `plugin-data/dsh-updater-npm/npm-logs/`;
3. **fi"},{"id":"p22s3","text":"lesystem activity** — npm's debug log may only be flushed at exit on Windows (in a measured
14-secon"},{"id":"p22s4","text":"d install it sat at 0 bytes for 12 of them), so the staging directory and its
`node_modules/` are wa"},{"id":"p22s5","text":"tched as well: extraction keeps writing files there."},{"id":"p23s1","text":"Only when **all three** are idle is the install treated as stuck; during a silent phase a
`[heartbea"},{"id":"p23s2","text":"t] …` line is appended every minute (into `last-run.log`)."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"- On a watchdog kill the log carries `[watchdog] …` and `[exit] …` lines, and the error states
wheth"},{"id":"p24s2","text":"er it was an **idle timeout** or the **total limit**, with the elapsed time — no more opaque `: npm`"},{"id":"p24s3","text":".
- The same policy covers staged installs, non-Windows in-place `npm install -g`, and source-tree

[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"### Plugin self-version and self-update gate"},{"id":"p26s1","text":"- The card shows **this plugin's own version** and compares it with the latest `dsh-updater-npm` on
"},{"id":"p26s2","text":"npm (`GET https://registry.npmjs.org/dsh-updater-npm/latest`, cached for 10 minutes).
- If the plugi"},{"id":"p26s3","text":"n itself is outdated, the card says so and shows a copyable command
(`dsh plugin --profile <your pro"},{"id":"p26s4","text":"file> add dsh-updater-npm@<latest>`). The "Update via npm" button is
disabled, and `/update` is refu"},{"id":"p26s5","text":"sed server-side with the same message.
- Reason: updating DSH is performed by the **currently runnin"},{"id":"p26s6","text":"g plugin code**, and an outdated
plugin's upgrade path may itself be unsafe (1.9.0, for example, sta"},{"id":"p26s7","text":"ged without `-g` on Windows and
lost every dependency after the swap).
- **Offline pass-through:** n"},{"id":"p26s8","text":"othing is blocked unless a newer plugin version is positively known, so
air-gapped or offline setups"},{"id":"p26s9","text":" are not locked out.
- Source-tree mode (`git pull`) is not gated, only hinted."},{"id":"p27s1","text":"### DSH Docs"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"- **Sync switch (off by default):** the "DSH Docs" card has an "Auto-sync official docs" toggle.

loaded"},{"id":"p28s3","text":". When on, the plugin syncs on first start (~217 files: English + Chinese `.zh.md`) and then
every 2"},{"id":"p28s4","text":"4 hours, and registers the tools. The switch state lives in
